newsitem.title: INDIA: TEXT - SEBI statement after board meeting.
newsitem.headline: TEXT - SEBI statement after board meeting.

text.p: Following is the text of a statement issued by the Securities and Exchange Commission of India (SEBI) after a board meeting on Monday in the Indian capital:
1. MUTUAL FUNDS
The Board today approved the revised Regulations for Mutual Funds, which are based on the Mutual Funds 2000 Report. Some of the salient features are as follows:

The revised regulation strongly emphasises on the governance aspect of mutual funds in the interest of investors, increases the responsibilities of trustees of the mutual funds in overseeing that the AMCs function in the interest of investors, enhances the level of investor protection and brings about empowerment of investors, as also lays down a Code of Conduct for best practices for the mutual funds to follow. The consent of investors will now have to be obtained by a mutual fund for any change in the "fundamental attributes" of a scheme, on the basis of which the unit holders have invested. The Regulations require that asset management companies exercise due diligence and care in managing the assets of a scheme as would be exercised by other persons engaged in the same business.

Provisions for portfolio disclosure, standardisation of accounting policies, valuation norms for Net Asset Value, pricing as recommended by the NAV Committee have been incorporated in the revised Regulations. Additional disclosures are required in respect of transactions by the schemes of Mutual Funds, with associates of sponsors, AMCs and trustees and also in respect of personal transactions of the key personnel of AMCs and trustees.

These regulations will now allow the mutual funds and asset management companies to innovate and structure schemes freely and several quantitative restrictions have been removed. The scope of activities of the asset management company has also been increased to other fund-based activities.

Payment of early bird incentive has also been allowed for schemes of mutual fund. However, such early bird incentives could be given only as interest payment for early investment with full disclosures. The offer document should disclose the source of funds from which the incentives are being paid.
The revised Regulation will be notified shortly and will come into effect thereafter.
2. VENTURE CAPITAL FUNDS

The Board approved the Regulations for Venture Capital. The Board recognised the venture capital is an activity which needs to be strongly encouraged. The Regulations are based on the Consultative Paper issued by SEBI on the subject some time back, and the comments received on the paper from the existing venture capital funds and other market participants. The Regulations allow only the institutional investors and high net worth individuals who are in a position to assess the investment risk in such funds and the quality of fund management to invest in such funds. The Regulations also allow Venture Capital funds to invest freely in unlisted companies, finance turnaround companies which are financially weak, and permits a venture capital fund to provide loans and other form of assistance, besides equity investments. The regulations will be notified shortly and will come into effect thereafter.
3. AMENDMENT TO REGULATIONS FOR CUSTODIANS

The existing Regulations for custodians require the custodians to have a minimum net worth of 500 million rupees. Some of the existing custodians who have been in existence for considerable period of time and have been providing services to a number of institutional investors have represented to SEBI seeking relaxation of this requirement, as their existing net worth falls far below 500 million rupees. The Board considered the request and decided to allow these custodians to increase their net worth to 500 million rupees in a phased manner over a period of five years. The Regulations are being amended in this respect and the amendment will be notified shortly.
DAVE COMMITTEE REPORT ON OTCEI
The recommendations of Dave Committee on OTCEI were discussed by the Board and under noted recommendations have been accepted:
Recommendation Number

1. All such companies which do not (i) have a three-year dividend paying record in the last five years and (ii) are not appraised or funded by FIs, be allowed to raise funds by listing on the OTCEI provided that they fulfil the listing criteria laid down by the OTCEI rules and regulations. These would include:
i. Being sponsored by a Member of the OTCEI, and
ii. Appointing at least two market makers to provide continuous liquidity to the stock - I Compulsory and I Additional Market Maker.
3. SEBI should remove the upper limit of 250 million rupees and allow all companies, irrespective of the size, to list on the OTCEI, on the same lines as the other stock exchanges.

5. OTCEI is already allowed to list Bought Out Deals (BODs) fulfilling all listing criteria. In addition, the Committee recommends that all BODs undertaken in the past as well as all future BODs -- which may not fulfil the three-year dividend paying record or the FI appraisal and funding criteria -- should also be allowed the facility of an Offer for Sale, listing and trading only on the OTCEI.

6. Equity shares of all unlisted companies be allowed to trade on the OTCEI. Besides providing an opportunity to make the stocks liquid and tradeable, such trading will provide a source of valuation for MFs, will facilitate inter-institutional trades, will enable placement of these shares with the FIIs who have now been permitted to subscribe to unlisted company stocks, etc. OTCEI may lay down a separate agreement that may be signed with such a company. The details in this regard would be worked out.

7. All such companies which are able to list on OTCEI in accordance with our recommendations Numbers 1, 2, 4 and 5 (which includes companies without a three-year dividend playing record, companies with a post-issue equity below 100 million rupees, companies not fulfilling the minimum shareholding criteria for listing and offers for sale in respect of BODs) should not be allowed to delist from the exchange for three years. The companies would be free to remain listed on the OTCEI or to list on any other exchange after the expiry of the three-year period.

8. The sponsors on the OTCEI should be permitted to give their appraised future projections in the issue document in cases where they are undertaking the market-making responsibility. In addition to FIs and Banks, sponsors should be allowed to give their future projections in the issue documents.
9. The detailed scheme for off-loading shares acquired under Bought Out Deals (BODs) under the proposed Tap system of offer given in Dave Committee Report was approved.

11. In order to provide greater depth and liquidity to the OTCEI market and to increase trading volumes, instruments like Futures and Options, Forward Contracts on Stocks, other forms of forward transactions, I Stock Lending etc might be encouraged on the OTCEI.

12. The proposal to shift from the "T-3" to a "T-5" settlement system where the pay-in takes place on the fifth day and the pay-out on the sixth day. However, the exchange should revert to at "T+3" system at a later date when the Banking system in India was more geared to support such a system.

13. Since in the permitted securities segment OTCEI was required to compete with the other exchanges on equal terms a weekly netting of trades should be allowed in the permitted securities segment of trading on the OTCEI. This would remove administrative bottlenecks and facilitate physical settlment of scrips on a nationwide basis. SEBI also agreed to allow the OTCEI to have a free hand in increasing the number of companies under the permitted securities and permitted debentures segment.

16. OTCEI managment should formulate a well thought out plan for upgradation of technology and evolving a suitable Management Structure which could cater to the wide scope of operations that is being contemplated for the exchange.

15. The graded system of market making as recommended by Dave Committee was also accepted. Under the new system up to 50 million rupees an initial market making inventory will be up to five percent and between 50 million rupees to 100 million rupees it will be of two percent.
14. The recommendations regarding greater participation by promoter financial institutions was also accepted.
SHORT SALES OF SECURITIES ON STOCK EXCHANGES
The Board considered the recommendations and decided that in principle short selling was required to be regulated and to begin with the following measures might be taken:-
a) Short seller should be asked to declare his position of short sale at the end of the day.
b) The Stock Exchange should impose appropriate margin on short sale.

The Board also decided that a group of experts might be set up to work out modalities to give effect to these decisions. The report of the group might be available in three weeks. This would be made public for comments. The Board also noted that Stock Lending Scheme was likely to be declared formally by Govt of India shortly. This factor too might be considered by the Group so that modalities would be worked out in a comprehensive manner.
